definitions.explanation: A plan or expectation about how things will turn out, often with an undertone of strategic thinking or personal calculation. Can be neutral or carry a slightly negative nuance of scheming.

examples.japanese: {目論見|もくろみ}が{外|はず}れた。
{彼|かれ}の{目論見|もくろみ}{通|どお}り、{事業|じぎょう}は{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: Just as he had planned, the business succeeded.

examples.japanese: {安|やす}く{仕入|しい}れて{高|たか}く{売|う}るという{目論見|もくろみ}は{見事|みごと}に{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: The scheme of buying cheap and selling high failed spectacularly.

notes:
USAGE:
Often implies a calculated expectation or strategic plan. When the plan fails, the common expression is {目論見|もくろみ}が{外|はず}れる. When it succeeds: {目論見|もくろみ}{通|どお}り. Can carry a slightly scheming or self-interested nuance depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目論見|もくろみ}が{外|はず}れる (one's plan backfires)
- {目論見|もくろみ}{通|どお}り (as planned/calculated)
- {目論見|もくろみ}が{当|あ}たる (one's plan hits the mark)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {計画|けいかく}: plan — neutral, formal, without the strategic or self-interested nuance
- {企|たくら}み: scheme, plot — stronger negative nuance, implies deceit
- {算段|さんだん}: strategy, plan — similar to {目論見|もくろみ} but more colloquial
